_meta.purpose: Companion to the CIS Controls v8 IG1 starter pack: the failure modes the essential safeguards exist to prevent. frameworkTag 'CIS', category 'Cyber Hygiene'.
_meta.origin: Moved verbatim from the inline `cisRiskTemplates` array in prisma/seed.ts (2026-11-08), so production receives it: prisma/seed.ts is never run on a deploy.
_meta.deliveredBy: scripts/seed-risk-templates.ts on every container start (scripts/entrypoint.sh), and prisma/seed.ts in dev, both through prisma/risk-template-fixtures.ts.

templates.title: Unmanaged Asset on the Network
templates.description: A device that is not on the asset inventory connects to the network and receives access without going through onboarding or hardening.

templates.title: Unauthorized or Unsupported Software in Use
templates.description: Software that is unapproved or past end-of-life runs on enterprise assets, expanding the attack surface with no patch path.

templates.title: Unpatched Known Vulnerability Exploited
templates.description: A known vulnerability is exploited because operating-system or application patches were not applied within the remediation window.

templates.title: Account Compromise via Weak Authentication
templates.description: An account is taken over because it lacked multi-factor authentication or reused a weak password.

templates.title: Malware Infection on Enterprise Assets
templates.description: Malicious code executes on assets due to missing anti-malware defenses, autorun exposure, or unfiltered email and web content.

templates.title: Unrecoverable Data After Incident
templates.description: Data cannot be restored after ransomware or failure because backups were missing, unprotected, or never tested.

templates.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
templates.description: Sensitive information is disclosed because it was not classified, access-controlled, or encrypted at rest and in transit.

templates.title: Successful Social-Engineering Attack
templates.description: A phishing or social-engineering attack succeeds because staff were not trained to recognize and report it.
